cohorts.summary: Players praise the polished action combat, attractive art style, and rewarding crafting systems despite overall negative sentiment.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features polished action combat, an attractive art style, and a rewarding crafting and gathering system.

citations.review_text:
It genuinely sucks writing a negative review for a game that finally turned itself into a really fun MMO, yet nobody should spend a dime on a world with a confirmed expiration date. Amazon Games completely revamped the leveling flow, polished the action combat, and made exploring the island of Aeternum feel super rewarding. Chopping down trees with echoing sound effects, swapping between classless weapon setups on the fly, and diving into expeditions gave it a great, tactile vibe that stood out from standard tab target MMOs.

Even with how solid the gameplay got, the servers are officially shutting down permanently on January 31, 2027, and the game has already been pulled from digital storefronts. If you stumble across a leftover physical disc or key somewhere, pass on it immediately. Pouring hours into an MMO just to watch your character and progress get wiped off the map in a couple of months simply is not worth it.

Your going to kill it! Really needs to be laws against doing this.  Your killing it and I hardly got to play it.  I don't dare play it any more either granted it's just going to die.  What I will say is what I played was good. The art style is lovely and it's got a great vibe.   But knowing they are just deleting it, it's already dead to me.

If companies can terminate a game at anytime, then I should be allowed a refund at anytime. This game had an incredible crafting system and incredible combat. Too bad it will be gone forever. Never trusting an Amazon game again.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system is a strong, highly polished aspect of the game, paired with a visually appealing world.

citations.review_text:
It genuinely sucks writing a negative review for a game that finally turned itself into a really fun MMO, yet nobody should spend a dime on a world with a confirmed expiration date. Amazon Games completely revamped the leveling flow, polished the action combat, and made exploring the island of Aeternum feel super rewarding. Chopping down trees with echoing sound effects, swapping between classless weapon setups on the fly, and diving into expeditions gave it a great, tactile vibe that stood out from standard tab target MMOs.

Even with how solid the gameplay got, the servers are officially shutting down permanently on January 31, 2027, and the game has already been pulled from digital storefronts. If you stumble across a leftover physical disc or key somewhere, pass on it immediately. Pouring hours into an MMO just to watch your character and progress get wiped off the map in a couple of months simply is not worth it.

New World has always felt like a game with a great foundation that never managed to become the MMO it could have been.

The combat is probably the strongest part of the game, and Aeternum itself is beautiful, but the actual MMO content gets repetitive very quickly. Questing relies heavily on the same kill and collect objectives, while enemy variety and meaningful PvE activities are nowhere near what you would expect from a game built around long-term progression.

The biggest problem is the endgame. Even with Expeditions, Mutations, PvP modes, Wars and territory control, there simply isn't enough variety to make the grind feel worthwhile for someone looking for a proper long-term PvE MMO experience.

New World also constantly gives me the feeling that its individual systems are more interesting than the game they are supposed to create together. Crafting, gathering, territory control and combat are all enjoyable on their own, but the overall progression loop becomes repetitive far too quickly.

And now, knowing that Amazon has stopped development and plans to shut the game down in January 2027, it's difficult to recommend investing hundreds of hours into it.

Great combat, beautiful world and some genuinely good MMO systems, but too repetitive, too shallow in several areas, and ultimately a disappointing MMO experience.

[b]Final Verdict: [/b] 4/10
